author: gobernment
body:
I've been seeing a few maps viable for use on Atlas, however I would like to make some quick pointers before the server continues further into adding them, as Atlas is still in development. Maps remain the same for how they're built, and I'd appreciate it if these questions could be taken into account: Ask yourself!

- Did you build your map at Y:0? If not, then this is bad for void deaths taking forever and it can cause lag when placing blocks. This can also make it easier for combat loggers, and it also has advantages (e.g non-flowing water) when constructing the map for mapmakers to use.
- Does your map have default terrain? This used to be a problem a while ago, but with the past few submissions for maps, it's occurred. All maps must have no default world generation, and must be void in all areas around the region of the map. This includes villages and flatlands.
- How laggy is your map to users? If you stack up on fences and non-full blocks in the map (as it's harder to render), it will cause problems with users trying to play your map and freeze them. You should try to keep non-full blocks to a minimum, as it takes the game longer to render them. If you want to add details like this, think about the gameplay first before moving forward with it.
- How easy is your map to learn? With Atlas comes translations and a lot of people able to play around the world that couldn't play before. Maps should be relatively easy to understand, and not have so many confusing routes but rather a tactical match that's fun for everyone that either doesn't need a language barrier (having to use signs to explain the map, in which a portuguese player wouldn't get) or is able for the foreign player to ask minimal questions in hopes of an answer. Basically, just make it easy to learn, and if it's a customized concept, try keeping it simple or familiar.

As well as those points, I am requesting maps for the following gamemodes:
- King of the Hill (Basically CTH, but with building and more support on majority)
- Free for All (Every man fends for himself, no teamwork allowed)
- Capture the Flag (Basically CTW, but with a flag instead [think boolean])

And also, the resource for learning is open on atlas.avicus.net, however be aware that some features are not entirely supported or are being revamped. Nothing is finalized until the update, but some basic resources can be found on the GitHub that may be helpful in assisting you with your XML.
